sectors.name: Financials
themes: Retail investor flows are increasingly concentrating in small-cap financial names like AHAP and RELI, creating durable momentum that persists until liquidity tightens or earnings disappoint.
Insurance subsector (ERIE, AMAR) is benefiting from structural premium growth and digital distribution, offering a defensive growth angle within financials.
Banking names (BDMN, 2881) are supported by stable NIMs and improving loan growth, but upside hinges on macro rate trajectory and credit quality, making them lower-beta core holdings.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in AHAP, RELI, and BDMN on strong retail-driven momentum, but keep exposure barbelled with ERIE and AMAR for insurance upside. Sector breadth is neutral, so avoid chasing INDO and 2881 after sharp moves; add on 2-3% dips. US financials' mild strength supports sentiment, yet local catalysts remain stock-specific. Trim any laggards to recycle into leaders.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's domestic coal demand is structurally rising due to new smelter and industrial park buildouts, making local coal players (ALKA, PSAB) less dependent on volatile export prices.
The ID/US performance gap (+1.86% vs +0.41%) reflects a persistent home-bias rotation into Jakarta-listed energy names, driven by rupiah stability and government energy security policies.
Mining services and infrastructure contractors (BAJA, MYOH) are benefiting from a capex supercycle in nickel and coal logistics, a durable driver as downstream processing mandates expand.
sectors.ai: Buy selectively into Indonesia's coal and energy complex on this momentum, but avoid chasing BYAN's +20% spike—it's likely a one-off rerating. Favor laggards with volume confirmation: ALKA, TRGP, and COAL still have upside if the WATCH signal flips to BUY. Trim any US-exposed names (TRGP) if the ID/US divergence widens. Position for a 2–4 week hold, then reassess.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable tariff deregulation and captive-market industrial demand are structurally lifting domestic IPP margins, favoring BATR and POWR over US peers.
US utility resilience (EIX, PCG, AWK) persists on grid-hardening capex and data-center load growth, but valuation compression risks rise if 10-year yields stay above 4.2%.
Climate-tech policy divergence—JETP funding acceleration in Indonesia versus US IRA rollback uncertainty—creates a relative-value tilt toward ASEAN solar and geothermal plays.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian renewables names (BATR, POWR) on domestic policy momentum and tariff reforms, while trimming US exposure (FSLR, SRE) as rate-cut expectations fade; watch for Q2 earnings confirmations and JETP disbursement catalysts before adding size.

sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap consumer names showing volume-driven re-rating (PADA, JARR, PGUN) as domestic demand stabilizes, but avoid chasing BEEF/AGAR momentum without earnings confirmation. Rotate into defensive staples with dividend support (SMGA, SIPD) for carry, and trim any exposure to US-linked names given the +0.20% lag. Position for Q3 festive seasonality by accumulating mid-cap FMCG with strong rural distribution now.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's accelerated national strategic project (PSN) pipeline, including toll roads and ports, is a durable demand driver for contractors like KIJA and YPAS through 2025-2026.
Telecom tower and data-center infrastructure (TOWR, PACK) benefits from structural digital adoption and 5G rollout, with recurring lease revenue insulating against construction cyclicality.
Domestic infrastructure outperformance vs US (-1.28%) reflects local monetary easing expectations and fiscal stimulus, favoring IDX-listed operators over global-linked peers in a rate-cut cycle.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian infrastructure names with confirmed order books (KIJA, TOWR) and avoid chasing speculative penny movers (ASLI, TEBE) lacking earnings support. The sector's aggregate gain masks divergence—domestic strength (+1.73%) vs US drag (-1.28%) favors local toll, tower, and data-center plays. Accumulate on dips toward 0.39% aggregate, targeting KIJA and TOWR for 3-6 month upside as government capex accelerates ahead of 2025 elections.

sectors.name: Healthcare
themes: Indonesia's hospital operators (RSGK, LABS) are consolidating mid-tier facilities, driving durable same-store revenue growth as private insurance penetration rises.
Global plasma-derived therapies (CSL) face a multi-year supply-demand gap, underpinning pricing power and margin expansion beyond cyclical recovery.
Obesity and metabolic drug pipelines (LLY, PODD) are shifting care delivery toward chronic disease management, creating durable demand for delivery devices and companion diagnostics.
sectors.ai: Healthcare's aggregate uptick is broad-based, not idiosyncratic, with global large-caps (LLY, ABBV, JNJ) and Indonesia's RSGK/LABS confirming a risk-on rotation into defensive growth. Buy pullbacks in CSL (plasma pricing power) and RSGK (domestic hospital consolidation), but trim PODD after its 5.96% pop—valuation is stretched. Position for sustained M&A and GLP-1 spillover into diagnostics and distribution.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's commodity export volumes, especially coal and nickel, remain a durable driver for haulage and port operators like RMKE and PORT, underpinned by sustained China demand and domestic smelter
E-commerce and last-mile delivery growth in tier-2/3 cities structurally lifts parcel logistics demand, favoring integrated players like SOCI and TMAS with network density and cold-chain expansion.
Government infrastructure spending on toll roads and ports reduces transit costs and improves asset utilization, a multi-year margin tailwind for listed logistics firms, particularly KJEN and MITI.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics selectively on domestic volume recovery and port efficiency gains; KJEN, PORT, and SOCI lead with earnings momentum while TMAS offers scale. US weakness is a headwind for global names, so overweight ID-centric operators. Add RMKE for coal haulage tailwind; trim TAXI on speculative froth. Position for Q3 volume data and tariff-driven rerating.

themes: Indonesia's digital advertising and OTT penetration continues to outpace GDP growth, structurally supporting DOOH and FAST platforms as advertisers shift budgets from traditional media.

Regulatory tailwinds for local content quotas and data localization are forcing global platforms to partner with domestic players, creating durable moats for Indonesian media incumbents.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum leaders (GRPH, MDIA, FAST, DOOH) on confirmed volume, but cap exposure at 5% each given WATCH signal and mixed US/ID divergence. Fade TGUK/FORU rallies into strength; rotate into FITT/ARCI as laggard catch-up plays. Tighten stops at 7% below entry; sector breadth remains fragile, so prioritize liquidity over conviction.

Layer-2 scaling and zero-knowledge proofs (POL, MATIC) structurally reduce transaction costs, boosting on-chain adoption in emerging markets.
Stablecoin infrastructure (STABLE, SKY) is becoming the settlement layer for cross-border remittances, a key Indonesia corridor.

Use POL/MATIC dips to accumulate for staking yield; avoid chasing STABLE/SKY until volume confirms. Hedge with AAVE as lending-rate proxy.
